newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains to replenish Brazil soybean regions - coops.
newsitem.headline: Rains to replenish Brazil soybean regions - coops.

text.p: Generalized rains were expected in the key Brazil soybean growing regions of Rio Grande do Sul and Parana overnight and would replenish soil moisture levels in areas which were becoming dry, producers said.

"Rains are forecast this evening for Rio Grande, Santa Catarina and Parana," said Nelson Costa of the Parana cooperatives organisation Ocepar. "We haven't had much rain in the last week but we still don't have any problems."

Temperatures in Parana were between 28 and 30 degrees Celsius creating normal conditions for the development of the soy crop, Costa said, adding that the state's crop should come in between 6.5 and seven million tonnes.

Variable weather in Rio Grande do Sul meant that some regions were getting a little dry, but tonight's rains should restore soil moisture levels in those areas to normal levels, said Jaime Tonon of the Santa Barbara cooperative.
"I don't see any risk of a lower soybean crop (because of a lack of rains)," he said. "There is no reason for market nervousness."
But he said the Brazil crop was unlikely to exceed 26 million tonnes because cash-strapped farmers had not been able to apply sufficient fertilizers during planting.
